subject: Pilot terms: pricing & benchmarking requests
messages:
From: Sarah Lewis <sarah.lewis@brightleaf.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T18:12:00Z
Subject: Pilot terms: pricing & benchmarking requests

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo — BrightLeaf liked the latency profile on the specialty inference path. We're preparing an internal pilot and legal asked me to surface a few commercial items up front so we can move quickly:

- Pilot length: 6 months, target start July 1.
- Discount: we'd like a 40% off list for the pilot term.
- Pricing protection: the business wants a right-to-match / MFN-like clause so that if Redwood offers a lower price for materially similar terms to another buyer in the next 12 months, BrightLeaf is entitled to the lower pricing for the remainder of the 12-month period.
- Benchmarking & publicity: BrightLeaf requires that Redwood not publish benchmarking results, case studies, or customer references without explicit written consent from BrightLeaf.
- Other: Legal will probably ask for the SOW to limit data retention and add a SOC 2 attestation.

Attaching our initial SOW for reference (SOW_BrightLeaf_v1.pdf). From a commercial standpoint, our VP of Innovation is pushing for preferential commercial protection because the pilot is being run against a competing internal initiative.

Can your team confirm whether these are acceptable as-is, or if Redwood will want carve-outs? If you need this routed to your deal desk or execs for signoff, please escalate — we'd like a decision by Jun 15 to keep our timeline.

Best,

Sarah Lewis
Director, Strategic Partnerships
BrightLeaf Health

Folks — forwarding BrightLeaf's ask. Key commercial asks summarized: 40% pilot discount, 12-month MFN / right-to-match, and a no-publishing/benchmark restriction.

Why this matters: BrightLeaf is a potential strategic account in health vertical; they run a multi-product procurement and the pilot could convert into a multi-region contract if we can move quickly. That said, MFN + restrictive publicity + deep discount is high-risk from a precedent perspective.

Attachments: their SOW and my draft term sheet (redwood-draft-term-sheet.pdf) with proposed counters.

Requested action: Priyom—deal desk review and recommended redlines + whether this needs Markus' exec signoff. If exec approval is needed, please call out specific ask (discount %, MFN term, publicity carve).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — thanks for the ping and the draft term sheet. High-level notes from Deal Desk:

1) Discount: 40% off list for a pilot is very aggressive relative to our current pilot comps. We can consider a concession but recommend capping at 30% for a short-duration pilot, with clear success criteria to trigger deeper discounts for expansion.

2) MFN / Right-to-Match: MFNs are one of the highest-risk clauses because they can cascade across deals and lock pricing. If we must agree to price protection, propose the following safe scoping:
   - Limit MFN to the exact set of SKUs used in the pilot (no portfolio-wide parity).
   - Limit duration to 6 months post-pilot effective date.
   - Exclude pre-existing deals and channel/reseller prices.
   - Require the customer to notify us and provide evidence of the lower pricing before any adjustment.

3) Benchmarking / publicity: a blanket "no publishes" request is overly broad. Suggested language: "No public case study, benchmark, or reference will be published without Customer's written consent; Redwood may present anonymized performance ranges in aggregate benchmarking materials provided no customer-identifiable information or logos are used."

4) Other commercial asks: consider a minimum committed spend ($50k) during the pilot or a defined POC acceptance criteria — that helps mitigate the revenue risk from the deep discount.

Recommendation: This package (40% + 12m MFN + publish ban) needs exec approval because it creates long-term precedent. If Markus approves the scoped redlines above (30% cap, 6m MFN scoped to pilot SKUs, consent-based publicity), Deal Desk will prepare a redlined term sheet for signature.

Please confirm BrightLeaf's flexibility on duration and whether they're willing to accept a committal or success metric.

--
Priyom Das
Manager, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot terms: pricing & benchmarking requests

Thanks for the summaries — I appreciate the risk callout, Priyom. I'm willing to approve a limited commercial concession to keep the pilot moving, provided Deal Desk scopes the language tightly and legal signs off on the redlines. Approvals below:

- Discount: approve up to 30% off list for the 6-month pilot, contingent on a $50k minimum committed spend during the pilot window and defined acceptance criteria in the SOW.

- MFN / Right-to-Match: approve only if all of the following are true:
   * MFN is limited to the specific pilot SKUs and usage profile (no portfolio or cross-product parity).
   * Duration capped at 6 months from pilot start (not 12).
   * Explicit carve-out for pre-existing customers and channel/reseller pricing.
   * Customer must submit a claim with evidence; price adjustments will be prospective only.

- Benchmarking/Publicity: do not accept a categorical ban. Replace with consent-based clause: Redwood may not publish customer-identifiable benchmarks or logos without written consent. BrightLeaf can request anonymization for any aggregate benchmarking materials.

Next steps: Priyom, please prepare a redlined term sheet reflecting the above and route to Legal (cc: me). Vanessa, please check with BrightLeaf on acceptance of the $50k minimum and 6-month MFN cap — if they push back hard on the MFN duration, escalate back to me with the commercial justification (ARR runway, strategic imperative).

Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
